passages.provision_quote: human trafficking of a minor, in violation of subdivision (c) of Section 236.1, except, with respect to a violation of paragraph (1) of subdivision (c) of Section 236.1, where the person who committed the offense was a victim of human trafficking, as described in subdivision (b) or (c) of Section 236.1, at the time of the offense; and
passages.note: Author of single-subject bill adding human trafficking of a minor to the serious-felony definition for Three Strikes purposes; a categorical sentencing enhancement for one crime, not a general toughest-penalties stance.

rows.reasoning: As the named author of SB 14 (2023-2024), Grove sponsored a single-subject bill that added human trafficking of a minor to the definition of 'serious felony' for all purposes, including the Three Strikes Law, imposing real sentencing consequences on that crime. This matches 'Breaking the law needs to have real consequences — accountability is the priority,' not the broader, unproven 'impose the toughest penalties the law allows,' and the categorical, instrument-wide enhancement excludes the individualized 'each situation is different' rung.
